title: Labour detail card 57101 — Zacharias Helman
subject: zacharias
note: Transfer to Magdeburg 23 July 1944; transfer to Auschwitz 6 October in a diagonal hand. Yellow line across the face marks a man sent away.

title: Buchenwald intake roster, page 8 — Zacharias 57101 and Michal 57103
note: Nominal roll of the 1,000 Hungarian-Jewish arrivals of 2 June 1944. Both coded Z4; Grünfeld, Herman at 57102 between them.

title: Buchenwald intake roster, page 6 — Lajos 56906
note: Two pages earlier in the same roll; lower number means earlier arrival.

title: Civil birth register, Bohdan, 1929 — Helen, entry 81
subject: helen

fields.Child: Helena, girl, Jewish. No surname is entered.
fields.Father: Named only in the remarks: Hellman Zacharias, resident of Bohdan, age 29, acknowledging the child as his own
fields.Signed: By the father, in his own hand

significance: Because the marriage was religious only, the state entered her under her mother's surname, so the child has no surname on the page. To trace her, look under Landó.

title: Civil birth register, Tiszabogdány, 1902 — David Helman, entry 44
subject: david

fields.Declarant: Helman Iczik, fuvaros (carter), resident of Tiszabogdány, born in Delatyn, age 51
fields.Mother: Dikter Faiga, napszámos (day labourer), born in Delatyn, age 37
fields.Remarks: 'Legitimate' struck out and 'natural' entered. Iczik declares direct knowledge of the child and acknowledges it as his own.
fields.Closing line: Read aloud to the declarant, who does not understand Hungarian, explained in a language he does understand, approved, and signed.
fields.Signed: Helman Itzik, in his own hand

significance: Both parents born in Delatyn, Galicia — the paternal origin. The religious-only marriage and the language barrier are already at work in 1902.

title: Civil birth register, Bohdan, 1927 — Hermina (Hinda) Helman, entry 48
subject: hinda

fields.Mother: Landó-ová Roža, at home, Bogdan, age 24, entered under her maiden name
fields.Father: In the remarks only: Zigmund Helman, resident of Bogdan, 26, povozník (carter), with right of domicile in Delatyn, Poland, acknowledging the child as his own
fields.Signed: Zigmund Helman, in his own hand

significance: Zigmund and Zacharias are the same man. Children filed under Landó. The pattern behind step two of the method: search the mother's maiden name.

title: 1921 Czechoslovak census, Bohdan, house 263 — the Helman household
note: Iczik (b.1849 Delatyn) and Feige (b.1867 Delatyn) with sons Misel 1886, Zigmond 1901, David 1902, Misel's wife Chaje, and six grandchildren.
significance: One sheet puts Misel (Miksa) in the same house as Zigmond (Zacharias) — turns two unknown men on a camp roster into a nephew and his uncle.

title: Yad Vashem Pages of Testimony — Miksa Helman, Adél née Petranker, and two sons
note: Submitted by surviving children filing from Israel in the 1990s.

title: Budapest survivor registration forms (Törzslap), 1945
note: In their own hands; place them in Budapest June 1945. Lajos registered 8 June; Michal wrote 'Helmán Mihály'.
